title: Who's Who: Clara Whitcomb
summary: Expedition correspondent whose work remains part of the record of modern Eidetics.
author: Who's Who Desk
paragraphs: The Correspondent adds Clara Whitcomb (born 1842) to its Who's Who of Eideticians, recording a expedition correspondent whose name still attends serious discussion of the Eidetic Stratum.

Whitcomb turned the Alderwick receiving hall’s cryptic daily readings into lucid newspaper reports. Her accounts of lost routes and disputed retrievals made Eideticians answer questions they had previously put off.
She travels with expeditions but keeps separate notebooks for what an instrument measured and what a witness believed.

For Alderwick readers, Clara Whitcomb stands not as an ornament to legend but as a figure whose work helps explain why Eideticians prize careful terms, repeatable evidence and a sober account of what remains unknown.
